claim: Oral inflammatory diseases such as apical periodontitis are common bacterial infectious diseases that may affect the periapical alveolar bone tissues.
source: Oral inflammatory diseases such as apical periodontitis are common bacterial infectious diseases that may affect the periapical alveolar bone tissues.
evidence: This is a general statement about apical periodontitis presented in the abstract without specific experimental data or citations in this sentence.

claim: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) play a primary role in the protective process that occurs simultaneously with inflammatory tissue destruction.
source: A protective process occurs simultaneously with the inflammatory tissue destruction, in which mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) play a primary role.
evidence: This claim is supported by the study's findings and established knowledge about MSC function.

claim: Oral diseases affect 3.5 billion people worldwide.
source: Oral diseases, particularly dental caries and periodontal diseases, affect 3.5 billion people worldwide (Disease et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Disease et al., 2018.

claim: Individuals with at least one tooth affected by AP comprise up to 52% of cases.
source: Individuals with at least one tooth affected by AP comprise up to 52% of cases, indicating that AP is a highly prevalent disease (Tibúrcio-Machado et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tibúrcio-Machado et al., 2021.

claim: Inflammation in the oral cavity can lead to destruction of surrounding periapical tissues and resorption of hard tissues.
source: Inflammation in the oral cavity can lead to destruction of surrounding periapical tissues and resorption of hard tissues, a consequence of the unbalanced interaction between infection and the immune response (Gazivoda et al., 2009; Márton and Kiss, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gazivoda et al., 2009 and Márton and Kiss, 2014.

claim: Active inflammation, tissue injury, and the protective process all occur simultaneously in the setting of chronic AP.
source: Active inflammation, the tissue injury and the protective process all occur simultaneously in the setting of chronic AP (Márton and Kiss, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Márton and Kiss, 2014.

claim: Polymorphonuclear leukocytes, lymphocytes, and monocyte/macrophages are important in periapical defense.
source: Importantly, there is a complex assemblage of immune cell types involved in the pathogenesis, highlighting the importance of polymorphonuclear leukocytes, lymphocytes, and monocyte/macrophages in periapical defense (Braz-Silva et al., 2019; Nair, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Braz-Silva et al., 2019 and Nair, 2004.

claim: MSCs exert immunomodulatory effects and have regenerative potential during oral inflammatory diseases.
source: Notably, an increasing number of studies report the involvement of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in the protective action that occurs during oral inflammatory diseases, whereby MSCs exert immunomodulatory effects and have regenerative potential (Li et al., 2014; Márton and Kiss, 2000; Nair, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2014; Márton and Kiss, 2000; and Nair, 2004.

claim: MSC markers such as CD44, CD73, CD90, CD106, and STRO-1 have been observed in human periapical inflammatory tissues.
source: MSC markers such as CD44, CD73, CD90, CD106, and STRO-1 have been observed in human periapical inflammatory tissues (Estrela et al., 2019; Liao et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Estrela et al., 2019 and Liao et al., 2011.

claim: Cells isolated from the inflamed periapical region were able to produce colony-forming unit-fibroblasts (CFU-Fs) with high-osteogenic capacity.
source: Cells isolated from the inflamed periapical region were able to produce colony-forming unit-fibroblasts (CFU-Fs) with high-osteogenic capacity.
evidence: This claim is presented as established knowledge without a specific citation in this sentence.

claim: Interference with MSC mobilization toward the periapex region in an AP mouse model led to enlargement of lesions, accompanied by decreased wound healing markers and increased inflammatory cytokines.
source: It is also reported that interference with MSC mobilization toward the periapex region in an AP mouse model led to enlargement of lesions, accompanied by decreased wound healing markers and increased inflammatory cytokines (Araujo-Pires et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Araujo-Pires et al., 2014.

claim: The combined libraries from healthy and AP alveolar bone contained 15,148 individual cells.
source: The combined libraries from healthy and AP alveolar bone contained 15,148 individual cells.
evidence: This is a direct report of the experimental data from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Seurat's unbiased cluster detection algorithm identified 15 distinct cell populations.
source: Seurat's unbiased cluster detection algorithm identified 15 distinct cell populations (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the computational analysis results shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: T cell, B cell, NK cell, macrophage, epithelial cell, and MSC had significantly increased frequency in AP samples.
source: T cell, B cell, NK cell, macrophage, epithelial cell, and MSC had significantly increased frequency in AP samples.
evidence: This claim is supported by the frequency analysis comparing AP and control samples shown in Figures 2A and 1D.

claim: Neutrophil, myeloid progenitor, monocyte, megakaryocyte, mast cell, HSC, and dendritic cell were markedly decreased in AP samples.
source: Neutrophil, myeloid progenitor, monocyte, megakaryocyte, mast cell, HSC, and dendritic cell were markedly decreased (Figures 2A and 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the frequency analysis comparing AP and control samples shown in Figures 2A and 1D.

claim: Neutrophils are important components in the acute phase of AP as a first line of defense.
source: Neutrophils are important components in the acute phase of AP as a first line of defense.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about neutrophil function in AP.

claim: The most significantly enriched genes in neutrophils were various proinflammatory chemokines and cytokines including Cxcl2, Ccl6, Nlrp3, and Il1b.
source: Single-cell differential expression analysis revealed that the most significantly enriched genes in neutrophils were various proinflammatory chemokines and cytokines. These included C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (Cxcl2), C-C motif chemokine ligand 6 (Ccl6), NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (Nlrp3), and Interleukin-1β (Il1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell differential expression analysis of the neutrophil cluster.

claim: Ccrl2 was upregulated in neutrophils during AP.
source: Notably, we found that C-C motif chemokine receptor like 2 (Ccrl2) was upregulated in neutrophils during AP (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Ccrl2 is responsible for the innate defense against pathogens and is involved in the regulation of neutrophil migration.
source: It is responsible for the innate defense against pathogens and is also involved in the regulation of neutrophil migration (Del Prete et al., 2017; Kolaczkowska and Kubes, 2013; Mantovani et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Del Prete et al., 2017; Kolaczkowska and Kubes, 2013; and Mantovani et al., 2011.

claim: Il6 production was present in mast cells, monocytes, and macrophages with the highest expression level in mast cells.
source: The production of Interleukin-6 (Il6) was present in these cell populations with the highest expression level in mast cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: IL-1β is a key mediator of host response to microbial infection and is associated with the persistence of AP.
source: The pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-1β is a key mediator of host response to microbial infection and is associated with the persistence of AP (Morsani et al., 2011; Ng et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Morsani et al., 2011 and Ng et al., 2008.

claim: Il1b transcripts were found in monocyte, macrophage, mast cell, and neutrophil, with macrophages having the highest Il1b expression.
source: We found Il1b transcripts in a series of cell types, such as monocyte, macrophage, mast cell, and neutrophil. Of these, macrophages had the highest Il1b expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Tnf was detected in monocyte, macrophage, mast cell, myeloid progenitor, neutrophil, and HSC, with the highest expression observed in the monocyte population.
source: Another major cytokine, tumor necrosis factor (Tnf; Cotti et al., 2014), was detected in immunoresponsive cell clusters, such as monocyte, macrophage, mast cell, myeloid progenitor, neutrophil, and HSC, with the highest expression observed in the monocyte population (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis shown in Figure 2B and cited to Cotti et al., 2014.

claim: Ifitm1 and Ifitm2 were upregulated in monocytes during AP.
source: Furthermore, gene signatures from monocytes showed that the interferon-induced transmembranes (IFITMs) protein 1 and 2 (Ifitm1 and Ifitm2; Figure 2E) were upregulated the most during AP.
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: IFITMs have been associated with signal transduction of anti-inflammation activity in the immune system.
source: These factors have been associated with signal transduction of anti-inflammation activity in the immune system (Yánez et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yánez et al., 2020.

claim: Ccl9 expression was upregulated in the monocyte population from AP.
source: We also detected upregulated expression levels of Ccl9 in the monocyte population from AP.
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis of the monocyte cluster.

claim: Ccl9 is involved in the survival of osteoclasts during the destruction of the periapical bone.
source: Ccl9 is an important cytokine and is involved in the survival of osteoclasts during the destruction of the periapical bone (Silva et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Silva et al., 2007.

claim: S100a9 and S100a11 had increased expression in the AP monocyte cluster.
source: Also, genes coding for pro-inflammatory calcium-binding S100 family proteins such as S100a9 and S100a11 had increased expression in the AP monocyte cluster (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Macrophages are capable of secreting pro- and anti-inflammatory substances which act on the development and repair of AP lesions.
source: Previous reports demonstrated that macrophages are capable of secreting pro- and anti-inflammatory substances which act on the development and repair of the AP lesions (Italiani and Boraschi, 2014; Shapouri-Moghaddam et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Italiani and Boraschi, 2014 and Shapouri-Moghaddam et al., 2018.

claim: Pro-inflammatory mediators including Cxcl2, Cxcl16, Il1a, and Ptgs2 were upregulated in macrophages from AP samples.
source: Indeed, several genes encoding pro-inflammatory mediators, including Cxcl2, Cxcl16, Il1a, and Ptgs2, were upregulated in macrophages from AP samples (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Anti-inflammatory-associated genes such as Ifitm1 and Ifitm2 were significantly increased in the AP macrophage cluster compared to control cells.
source: Expression of anti-inflammatory-associated genes such as Ifitm1 and Ifitm2 was significantly increased in the AP macrophage cluster compared to control cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis of the macrophage cluster.

claim: Fcgr2b was markedly upregulated in macrophages from AP samples.
source: Furthermore, Fcγ receptor IIB (Fcgr2b) was markedly upregulated in macrophages from AP samples.
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis of the macrophage cluster.

claim: Fcgr2b is expressed in most tissue-resident macrophages and functions to inhibit Fcγ-dependent phagocytosis.
source: Fcgr2b is expressed in most tissue-resident macrophages (Gautier et al., 2012) and functions to inhibit Fcγ-dependent phagocytosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gautier et al., 2012.

claim: Fcgr2b inhibits release of cytokines such as IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1α, as well as neutrophil chemotactants.
source: It also inhibits release of cytokines such as IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1α, as well as neutrophil chemotactants (Clatworthy and Smith, 2004; Espéli et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Clatworthy and Smith, 2004 and Espéli et al., 2016.

claim: Apoe expression was significantly increased in the macrophage population during AP.
source: In addition, expression of Apolipoprotein E (Apoe), which can suppress the pro-inflammatory response (Jofre-Monseny et al., 2007), was significantly increased in the macrophage population (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2C and cited to Jofre-Monseny et al., 2007.

claim: Apoe can suppress the pro-inflammatory response.
source: In addition, expression of Apolipoprotein E (Apoe), which can suppress the pro-inflammatory response (Jofre-Monseny et al., 2007), was significantly increased in the macrophage population (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jofre-Monseny et al., 2007.

claim: T and B lymphocytes comprise the majority of the inflammatory infiltrate in AP.
source: T and B lymphocytes comprise the majority of the inflammatory infiltrate in AP (Graunaite et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Graunaite et al., 2012.

claim: Inflammatory-associated genes such as Srgn, Emb, Ctla4, and Il7r were significantly increased in expression in the AP T cell population.
source: A significant increase in the expression of inflammatory-associated genes, such as Srgn, Emb, Ctla4, and Il7r could be observed in the AP T cell population (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Inflammation-responsive genes (Fth1, Ftl1, Ebf1, and mt-Nd5) were upregulated in the AP B lymphocytes cluster.
source: In the AP B lymphocytes cluster, inflammation-responsive genes (Fth1, Ftl1, Ebf1, and mt-Nd5) were upregulated (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Lars2 was significantly upregulated in T and B lymphocytes during AP.
source: Interestingly, Lars2, the gene encoding a mitochondrial leucyl tRNA synthase (Carminho-Rodrigues et al., 2020; 't Hart et al., 2005), was significantly upregulated in T and B lymphocytes, indicating changes in mitochondrial metabolism in both clusters.
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis and citations to Carminho-Rodrigues et al., 2020 and 't Hart et al., 2005.

claim: Lars2 encodes a mitochondrial leucyl tRNA synthase.
source: Interestingly, Lars2, the gene encoding a mitochondrial leucyl tRNA synthase (Carminho-Rodrigues et al., 2020; 't Hart et al., 2005), was significantly upregulated in T and B lymphocytes, indicating changes in mitochondrial metabolism in both clusters.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Carminho-Rodrigues et al., 2020 and 't Hart et al., 2005.

claim: Markers of osteoclast and osteoclast precursors were highly expressed in the clusters of monocyte and macrophage.
source: Markers of osteoclast and osteoclast precursors were highly expressed in the clusters of monocyte and macrophage (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Inflammation related immune reactions and bone resorption activity were significantly enriched in macrophage cluster.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis showed that inflammation related immune reactions and bone resorption activity were significantly enriched in macrophage cluster (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the GO analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The monocyte cluster differentiated into the macrophage cluster.
source: The results showed that the monocyte cluster differentiated into the macrophage cluster (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Osteoclastic genes such as Ctsk, Acp5, Mmp9, Atp6v0d2, and Dcstamp were progressively elevated during the monocyte to macrophage trajectory.
source: During this trajectory, the gene expression pattern across pseudotime showed that osteoclastic genes, such as Ctsk, Acp5, Mmp9, Atp6v0d2, and Dcstamp, were progressively elevated (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Mature osteoclasts were differentiated from monocyte/macrophage lineage and contributed to inflammatory bone resorption during AP.
source: Of note, we have observed a branch which was highly positive for Ctsk and Acp5 (Figure 3H), indicating the mature osteoclasts were differentiated from monocyte/macrophage lineage and contributed to inflammatory bone resorption during AP.
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Markers of osteoclast and osteoclast precursors were significantly upregulated in bulk RNA-seq analysis of mandibular samples from mice with AP.
source: We have also analyzed the expression of osteoclast related genes using the bulk RNA-seq library built on mandibular samples extracted from mice with AP. Markers of osteoclast and osteoclast precursors were significantly upregulated, confirming the osteoclasts activity in the inflammatory-related bone lesion (Figure 3I).
evidence: This claim is supported by the bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: There is a close interaction among MSC, macrophage, and dendritic cells under homeostasis conditions.
source: We identified a close interaction among MSC, macrophage, and dendritic cells under homeostasis conditions (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the CellphoneDB analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A similarly close communication was found among MSC, macrophage, and dendritic cells under inflammatory conditions.
source: A similarly close communication was found among MSC, macrophage, and dendritic cells under inflammatory conditions (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the CellphoneDB analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: AP is associated with an overall decrease in cellular interactions.
source: The results suggested that AP is associated with an overall decrease in cellular interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the CrossTalkeR analysis comparing AP and control samples.

claim: MSC intercellular communication with mast cells and monocytes is upregulated during AP and accompanied by the highest number of interactions within MSCs themselves.
source: However, MSC intercellular communication with mast cells and monocytes is upregulated and accompanied by the highest number of interactions within MSCs themselves (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the CrossTalkeR analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Inflammatory-related proteins (Lgals9, Tnf, and Ccl4), extracellular matrix protein (Fn1), and protein involved in biomineralization (Spp1) were among the highest interactions.
source: Next, we ranked the individual ligands by the number of their interactions. Inflammatory-related proteins (Lgals9, Tnf, and Ccl4), extracellular matrix protein (Fn1), and protein involved in biomineralization (Spp1) were among the highest interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the ligand ranking analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Tgfb1, Vegfb, and Vegfa were in the top 10 most abundant ligands.
source: Also, Tgfb1, Vegfb, and Vegfa were in the top 10 most abundant ligands (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ligand ranking analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Inflammation associated genes (Tnf/neutrophil, Ccl3/mast cell, Ccl3/monocyte, and Il1b/macrophage) and matrix related genes (Sele/MSC, Fn1/MSC, and Fn1/monocyte) were the most influential ligands during AP when compared to control state.
source: Bar plots were also generated to display the top 10 upregulated gene/cell pairs, showing that inflammation associated genes (Tnf/neutrophil, Ccl3/mast cell, Ccl3/monocyte, and Il1b/macrophage) and matrix related genes (Sele/MSC, Fn1/MSC, and Fn1/monocyte) were the most influential ligands during AP when compared to control state (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the gene-cell prioritization analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Sele was primarily directed by MSC toward the MSC cluster via multiple receptors including Glg1, Selplg, and Cd44.
source: The results indicated that Sele was primarily directed by MSC toward the MSC cluster via multiple receptors including Glg1, Selplg, and Cd44.
evidence: This claim is supported by the Sankey plot analysis shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Fn1 was secreted by MSC, monocyte, macrophage, and mast cells toward MSCs.
source: Moreover, Fn1 was secreted by MSC, monocyte, macrophage, and mast cells toward MSCs (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the Sankey plot analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Sele and Fn1 are important cell adhesion molecules that mediate cell homing and migration.
source: Of note, Sele and Fn1 are important cell adhesion molecules that mediate cell homing and migration (Frenette et al., 1998; To and Midwood, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Frenette et al., 1998 and To and Midwood, 2011.

claim: MSCs represented 1.76% of total identified cells.
source: MSCs represented the non-immune cell population in alveolar bone, constituting 1.76% of total identified cells.
evidence: This is a direct report of the frequency of MSCs in the total cell population.

claim: The MSC population could be decomposed into four subclusters.
source: This cell population could be decomposed into four subclusters (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the clustering analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The most dominant MSC subcluster was characterized by high expression of Prrx1, Pdgfrb, Cxcl12, Angpt1, Runx2, and Sp7, and was classified as MSC_osteolineage cells (OLCs).
source: The most dominant subcluster was characterized by high expression of Prrx1, platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (Pdgfrb), and hematopoiesis supporting factors such as C-X-C motif chemokine 12 (Cxcl12) and angiopoietin (Angpt1). It was also characterized by osteogenic-related markers, such as Runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2), Sp7, and was thus classified as the MSC_osteolineage cells (OLCs).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis of the MSC subclusters.

claim: The other MSC subclusters were identified as MSC_endothelial (Cdh5+), MSC_neurological (Plp1+), and MSC_inflammatory (S100a8/S100a9+).
source: The other subclusters were identified as MSC_endothelial (Cdh5+), MSC_neurological (Plp1+), and MSC_inflammatory (S100a8/S100a9+; Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: The cell composition of the MSC cluster indicated an expansion of MSC_inflammatory subcluster during AP, whereas the MSC_neurological subcluster was reduced.
source: The cell composition of the MSC cluster indicated an expansion of MSC_inflammatory subcluster during AP, whereas the MSC_neurological subcluster was reduced (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the frequency analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Lineage tracing experiments showed increased numbers of Prrx1+ and Sp7+ MSC_OLCs as well as upregulated Gli1+ and Lepr+ periodontal ligament stem cells (PDLSCs) in AP lesions.
source: Of note, we performed lineage tracing experiments using Prrx1Cre, Sp7Cre, LeprCre, and Gli1CreER transgenic mouse models to identify stem cells in alveolar bone and the surrounding periodontal tissues (Cui et al., 2020; Fan et al., 2022; Men et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2020). The results suggested increased numbers of Prrx1+ and Sp7+ MSC_OLCs as well as upregulated Gli1+ and Lepr+ periodontal ligament stem cells (PDLSCs) in AP lesions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the lineage tracing data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and citations to Cui et al., 2020; Fan et al., 2022; Men et al., 2020; and Zhang et al., 2020.

claim: MSC_OLCs were enriched for ossification, connective tissue development, skeletal system development, and osteoblast differentiation.
source: MSC_OLCs were enriched for ossification, connective tissue development, skeletal system development, and osteoblast differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by the GO enrichment analysis of MSC subclusters.

claim: MSC_endothelial cells displayed enrichment for angiogenesis, blood vessel morphogenesis, and endothelium development.
source: MSC_endothelial cells displayed enrichment for angiogenesis, blood vessel morphogenesis, and endothelium development.
evidence: This claim is supported by the GO enrichment analysis of MSC subclusters.

claim: MSC_neurological cells were enriched for myelination, ensheathment of neurons, and axon ensheathment.
source: MSC_neurological cells were enriched for myelination, ensheathment of neurons, and axon ensheathment.
evidence: This claim is supported by the GO enrichment analysis of MSC subclusters.

claim: MSC_inflammatory cells were enriched for regulation of protein export from nucleus, electron transport chain, mitochondrial ATP synthesis coupled electron transport, and oxidative phosphorylation.
source: GO term analyses suggested highly specialized functional features of MSC_inflammatory cells, including regulation of protein export from nucleus, electron transport chain, mitochondrial ATP synthesis coupled electron transport, and oxidative phosphorylation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: There was a significant difference in the single cell expression levels of OLC-associated transcripts such as Sparc, Col1a1, Col1a2, Bglap, Bglap2, and Postn in the MSC cluster between AP and control groups.
source: Among the top upregulated genes, we observed a significant difference in the single cell expression levels of OLC-associated transcripts, such as secreted protein that is acidic and rich in cysteine (Sparc), Col1a1, Col1a2, Bglap, Bglap2, and Postn, accompanied by a trend toward increased Runx2 expression (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Sparc, Col1a1, Col1a2, and Runx2 were significantly upregulated in AP as verified by real-time quantitative PCR and bulk RNA sequence analysis.
source: We verified their expressions by real-time quantitative PCR and bulk RNA sequence analysis. The results revealed that Sparc, Col1a1, Col1a2, and Runx2 were significantly upregulated, and Bglap tended to increase during AP (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR and bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A, B.

claim: There were increased numbers of Sparc+/Sp7+ or Col1+/Sp7+ cells embedded in the bone matrix in the AP group.
source: In vivo experiments confirmed the upregulated expression of osteogenic-related markers, such as Sparc and Col1a1 in the AP group. There were increased numbers of Sparc+/Sp7+ or Col1+/Sp7+ cells embedded in the bone matrix, implying the protective function of MSC to differentiate into osteoprogenitors and osteoblasts under AP conditions (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: Gli1+ PDLSCs migrated to AP lesions and differentiated into Runx2+-osteoblasts.
source: Lineage tracing analysis further revealed that Gli1+ PDLSCs migrated to AP lesions and differentiated into Runx2+-osteoblasts (Figure 5G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the lineage tracing data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Inflammation could stimulate the progenitor cells in the adjacent bone and periodontium differentiating toward osteoblasts, thus contributing to the protective actions during AP.
source: Moreover, using LeprCre;Rosa26Ai14;Col2.3-GFP mouse model, we identified more Lepr+/Col2.3+ cells in the alveolar bone, confirming that inflammation could stimulate the progenitor cells in the adjacent bone and periodontium differentiating toward osteoblasts, thus contributing to the protective actions during AP (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by the lineage tracing data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Starting with MSC_endothelial cells, MSCs were able to differentiate into MSC_OLCs and MSC_neurological cells, with MSC_inflammatory cells corresponding to an intermediate state.
source: We then examined the characteristics of the MSCs with respect to their specific states. We plotted the estimated pseudotime of each cluster cell in the state space, and the results indicate that starting with MSC_endothelial cells, MSCs were able to differentiate into MSC_OLCs and MSC_neurological cells. MSC_inflammatory cells may correspond to an intermediate state (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: MSC_OLCs in state 3, as osteogenic primed MSCs, exhibited the highest tendency toward osteoblastic differentiation with upregulated expressions of Col1a1, Col1a2, Bglap, Spp1, and Postn.
source: Interestingly, MSC_OLCs in state 3, as osteogenic primed MSCs, exhibited the highest tendency toward osteoblastic differentiation with upregulated expressions of Col1a1, Col1a2, Bglap, Spp1, and Postn (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The MSC_OLCs population in state 3 increased significantly in the AP group.
source: Notably, this MSC population increased significantly in the AP group (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the frequency analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Osteogenic genes such as Sparc, Col1a1, Col1a2, and Bglap were upregulated during inflammation when compared to the homeostatic state.
source: A comparison of the dynamics of the gene expression pattern across pseudotime revealed upregulation of osteogenic genes such as Sparc, Col1a1, Col1a2, and Bglap during inflammation when compared to the homeostatic state (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime gene trajectory analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The expressions of SPARC, COL3A1, and RUNX2 were significantly enhanced in alveolar bone from patients with AP.
source: The expressions of SPARC, COL3A1, and RUNX2 were significantly enhanced in alveolar bone from patients with AP, accompanied by increases in SPP1 and BGLAP (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR data from human samples shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Immunostaining detected a more extensive distribution of SPARC, BGLAP, and RUNX2 in AP alveolar bone marrow.
source: Moreover, immunostaining detected a more extensive distribution of SPARC, BGLAP, and RUNX2 in AP alveolar bone marrow, confirming higher osteogenic potential under AP conditions (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the immunofluorescence data from human samples shown in Figure 7B–D.

claim: Immune cells accounted for the majority of the cell components in the mandibular microenvironment.
source: Immune cells accounted for the majority of the cell components in the mandibular microenvironment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell type composition analysis.

claim: The MSC population had the most interaction with itself and other immune cells under inflammatory conditions.
source: Cell-to-cell communication analysis revealed that among the multiple cell types, the MSC population had the most interaction with itself and other immune cells under inflammatory conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the CellphoneDB and CrossTalkeR analysis.

claim: MSCs were stimulated by inflammation and differentiated toward osteogenic lineage cells in order to protect the alveolar bone.
source: We used the expression profile and the pseudotime analysis to demonstrate that MSCs were stimulated by inflammation and differentiated toward osteogenic lineage cells in order to protect the alveolar bone.
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime analysis and expression profiling data.

claim: Cxcl2 is one of the most critical chemokines for neutrophil recruitment at a site of inflammation.
source: Cxcl2 was detected in endodontic infections (de Gomes and Herrera, 2018) and is one of the most critical chemokines for neutrophil recruitment at a site of inflammation (Kobayashi, 2008; Silva et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to de Gomes and Herrera, 2018; Kobayashi, 2008; and Silva et al., 2007.

claim: Increased levels of Cxcl2 have been reported to be associated with bone-resorptive activity in periapical lesions.
source: Increased levels of Cxcl2 have been reported to be associated with bone-resorptive activity in periapical lesions (AlShwaimi et al., 2013), highlighting the pro-inflammatory role of Cxcl2 in the progression of AP.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to AlShwaimi et al., 2013.

claim: Ifitm1 and Ifitm2 encode for a family of small transmembrane proteins localized in the plasma and endolysosomal membranes.
source: Ifitm1 and Ifitm2 encode for a family of small transmembrane proteins localized in the plasma and endolysosomal membranes.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about Ifitm proteins.

claim: Ifitm1 and Ifitm2 can be stimulated by interferons and exert an anti-inflammatory function in innate and adaptive immunity.
source: Although the function of Ifitm has not been assessed in the context of AP, there is considerable evidence suggesting that Ifitm1 and Ifitm2 can be stimulated by interferons and exert an anti-inflammatory function in innate and adaptive immunity (Liao et al., 2019; Yánez et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Liao et al., 2019 and Yánez et al., 2020.

claim: MSCs do not express S100a8/a9 under healthy conditions but upregulate its expression in disease states.
source: Recent studies have found that although MSCs do not express S100a8/a9 under healthy conditions, they do upregulate its expression in disease states (Leimkühler et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Leimkühler et al., 2021.

claim: S100a8/a9 might be a candidate for detecting an inflammatory-associated MSC state in AP.
source: The higher S100a8/a9 expression in the MSC_inflammatory cell subcluster suggests that S100a8/a9 might be a candidate for detecting an inflammatory-associated MSC state in AP.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data and literature.

claim: Sparc is one of the most abundant non-collagenous proteins expressed in bone.
source: Sparc is one of the most abundant non-collagenous proteins expressed in bone.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about Sparc.

claim: Sparc has a critical role in osteoblast differentiation, procollagen processing, and assembly as well as mineralization.
source: It has a critical role in osteoblast differentiation, procollagen processing, and assembly as well as mineralization (Rosset and Bradshaw, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rosset and Bradshaw, 2016.

claim: SPARC mutations have been identified in patients with osteogenesis imperfecta and idiopathic osteoporosis.
source: SPARC mutations have been identified in patients with osteogenesis imperfecta and idiopathic osteoporosis (Delany et al., 2008; Mendoza-Londono et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Delany et al., 2008 and Mendoza-Londono et al., 2015.

claim: Sparc null mice exhibit decreased osteoblast number and activity along with reduced bone formation rate.
source: Sparc null mice exhibit decreased osteoblast number and activity along with reduced bone formation rate (Delany et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Delany et al., 2003.

claim: SPARC is highly expressed in human periodontal MSCs.
source: Recent research using scRNA-seq revealed high levels of SPARC expression in human periodontal MSCs, highlighting the potential role of SPARC in oral MSC populations (Pagella et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pagella et al., 2021.

claim: Overexpressed Sparc is observed in inflammatory pulp cells, experimental glomerulonephritis, and ovarian cancer associated inflammation.
source: Notably, Sparc is also a molecule closely related to inflammation. Overexpressed Sparc is observed in inflammatory pulp cells, experimental glomerulonephritis, and ovarian cancer associated inflammation (Dimitrova-Nakov et al., 2014; Pichler et al., 1996; Said et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dimitrova-Nakov et al., 2014; Pichler et al., 1996; and Said et al., 2008.

claim: Both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory properties of Sparc have been reported.
source: Both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory properties of Sparc have been reported (Said et al., 2008; Sangaletti et al., 2011; Tanaka et al., 2018; Toba et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Said et al., 2008; Sangaletti et al., 2011; Tanaka et al., 2018; and Toba et al., 2015.

claim: The MSC population was stimulated by inflammation and underwent osteogenesis with a significant function in bone matrix assembly and mineralization.
source: Given the upregulation of Sparc observed in AP mouse models and human patients, we believe that the MSC population was stimulated by inflammation and underwent osteogenesis with a significant function in bone matrix assembly and mineralization, thus serving as an important protective component in healing the bone lesions in inflammation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the study's findings and the known functions of Sparc.

claim: The evoked-bleeding step in revascularization procedures for regenerative endodontic treatment leads to a substantial influx of MSCs.
source: The evoked-bleeding step in revascularization procedures for regenerative endodontic treatment leads to a substantial influx of MSCs, confirming the existence and regenerative properties of MSCs in the periapical region.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about MSCs in endodontic treatment.

claim: MSCs were found to be present in inflamed periapical tissues in adult patients with AP.
source: More importantly, MSCs were found to be present in inflamed periapical tissues in adult patients with AP.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Human apical papilla and its resident cells from teeth with pulp necrosis and AP could survive and retain their stemness in an inflammatory environment.
source: Evidence showed that human apical papilla and its resident cells from teeth with pulp necrosis and AP could survive and retain their stemness in an inflammatory environment (Chrepa et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chrepa et al., 2017.

claim: MSCs found in the periapical region were positive for typical stem cell markers such as STRO-1, CD90, CD73, CD105, CD146, and SOX2.
source: MSCs found in the periapical region were positive for typical stem cell markers, such as STRO-1, CD90, CD73, CD105, CD146, and SOX2 (Chrepa et al., 2015; Estrela et al., 2017; Liao et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chrepa et al., 2015; Estrela et al., 2017; and Liao et al., 2011.

claim: Progenitors from the periapical region were able to form CFU-Fs, illustrating a typical MSC feature.
source: These progenitors were able to form CFU-Fs, illustrating a typical MSC feature.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about MSC characteristics.

claim: The proportion of MSC_inflammatory cells in AP was higher and accompanied by significantly increased expression of S100a8/a9.
source: Importantly, we noted that the proportion of MSC_inflammatory cells in AP was higher and accompanied by significantly increased expression of S100a8/a9.
evidence: This claim is supported by the frequency and expression analysis of MSC subclusters.

claim: S100a8/a9 is involved with Ca2+ binding which is significantly increased during inflammatory processes.
source: These factors are involved with Ca2+ binding which is significantly increased during inflammatory processes (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2018.

claim: The bone lesions of AP patients receiving RCT usually fully recovered with resolution of radiolucency after the inflammation is controlled in apical area.
source: The bone lesions of AP patients receiving RCT usually fully recovered with resolution of radiolucency after the inflammation is controlled in apical area (Soares et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Soares et al., 2006.

claim: The healing of AP lesion is highly correlated with the osteogenic potential of inflamed MSCs.
source: The healing of AP lesion is highly correlated with the osteogenic potential of inflamed MSCs (Lin et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lin et al., 2009.

claim: The overall size of the MSC population was significantly increased during AP.
source: The overall size of the MSC population was significantly increased and was accompanied by upregulated expression of key osteogenic-related genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the frequency analysis of cell populations.

claim: Pseudotime analysis detected a specific state progression toward osteogenesis in the MSC cluster.
source: Moreover, pseudotime analysis detected a specific state progression toward osteogenesis in the MSC cluster.
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The numerical changes in the osteogenic state were statistically higher in AP samples when compared to control.
source: The numerical changes in this state were statistically higher in AP samples when compared to control.
evidence: This claim is supported by the frequency analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: MSCs in the osteogenic state harbored the highest osteoblastic differentiation potential, along with upregulated expressions of Sparc, Col1a1, Col1a2, Runx2, and Bglap.
source: MSCs in this state harbored the highest osteoblastic differentiation potential, along with upregulated expressions of Sparc, Col1a1, Col1a2, Runx2, and Bglap.
evidence: This claim is supported by the pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 6C and E.

claim: Upregulated SPARC, RUNX2, COL3A1, and BGLAP were observed in alveolar bone from human patients with AP.
source: We show, for the first time, upregulated SPARC, RUNX2, COL3A1, and BGLAP in alveolar bone from human patients with AP.
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR and immunofluorescence data from human samples shown in Figure 7.

claim: Sparc was the most upregulated marker in the MSC population from AP samples.
source: It is notable that Sparc was the most upregulated marker in the MSC population from AP samples.
evidence: This claim is supported by the differential expression analysis of the MSC cluster.
